1.  Sri Rahul Srivastava, learned counsel for C.B.I. apprised the Court that he has received the instructions, therefore, instant anticipatory bail application may be finally disposed off.

2. Heard Ms. Kritika Singh, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Shikhar Tandon, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rahul Srivastava, learned counsel for C.B.I.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R. No.
RC/DST/2015/A/0004 dated 30.07.2015, under Sections120B IPC read with 409, 420, 466, 467,
469, 471 IPC and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of P.C. Act, Police Station STF, CBI New Delhi with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail during trial.

entities.text: Police Station STF, CBI New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, applicant was Junior Engineer in NOIDA Development Authority and he was not named in the FIR, which was lodged in the year 2015 but during investigation on the basis of false allegation he has been made accused.
5. She further submits, however, almost ten years have been passed since the lodgment of the FIR but till date CBI could not file the charge-sheet in the present matter.

6. She further submits, when in the year 2022 applicant filed instant anticipatory bail application then co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 03.01.2025 was pleased to enlarge him on interim anticipatory bail and till date applicant is on interim anticipatory bail.
7. She further submits, applicant is not having any criminal history.

She further submits, therefore,
considering the facts of the case, the interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicant vide order dated 03.01.2025 may be confirmed.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for C.B.I. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Applicant was posted as Junior Engineer in NOIDA Development Authority and as per allegation he along with other accused misappropriated the public fund but it reflects, FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2015 and applicant was not named in the FIR and during investigation he has been made accused in the present matter.
11. Further, surprisingly almost ten years have been passed since the FIR but till date investigation of the case could not be completed.

Further, record also suggests that instant anticipatory bail application is pending since the year 2022 and on 03.01.2025 applicant has been enlarged on interim anticipatory bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court and there is no allegation that he misused the liberty granted to him.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicant vide order dated 03.01.2025 is hereby confirmed.
The applicant- Pramod Kumar shall remain on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial on the same condition as imposed by this Court vide order dated 03.01.2025.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

15. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
